item.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation has critical issues with data population. The hooks are set up correctly but don't properly capture and populate HTTP/2 request/response data from the underlying HTTP/2 connections. The tests show that records are created but they're missing essential data like method, URL, status code, and content.
item.contract: Fix the HTTP/2 hook implementation to properly capture and populate HTTP/2 request and response data (method, URL, status code, headers, content) during the HTTP/2 connection lifecycle. The hooks must properly integrate with HTTP/2 connection handlers to populate all record fields after the request completes.

item.description: The HTTP2Record implementation has incomplete HTTP/2 header parsing. The current implementation assumes that headers are available in a particular format, but HTTP/2 headers are binary-encoded frames that need to be properly decoded before being processed.
item.contract: Improve the HTTP2Record implementation to properly parse HTTP/2 binary headers from the underlying HTTP/2 connection. The implementation should extract pseudo-headers (:method, :path, :authority, :status) and regular headers correctly from the binary frame data.

item.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation doesn't properly handle asynchronous HTTP/2 client methods. The async methods are being decorated but they aren't properly integrated with the HTTP/2 connection handler that should populate the record data after the HTTP/2 transaction completes.
item.contract: Ensure that the HTTP/2 hook properly handles both synchronous and asynchronous HTTP/2 client methods by implementing proper data population mechanisms that work with the underlying HTTP/2 connection lifecycle.

item.description: The HTTP2Record implementation has incomplete URL construction logic. The URL construction logic in the url property doesn't properly handle cases where pseudo-headers are not available or malformed, causing records to be created with invalid URLs.
item.contract: Enhance the URL construction logic in HTTP2Record to properly handle various scenarios where pseudo-headers might be missing or malformed, ensuring all records have valid URLs for testing.

item.description: The HTTP2Record implementation doesn't handle HTTP/2 exception cases properly. When HTTP/2 requests fail, the exception information isn't properly captured and stored in the record.
item.contract: Update the HTTP2Record implementation to properly capture and store exception information when HTTP/2 requests fail, ensuring that exception records are created with proper error information.
